summary: A 1970 response by Steve Crocker to RFC 67, which proposed changing the host-IMP specification. It is part of the discussion.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 73 responds to a suggested protocol change by recommending that sites implement the current protocol first. The author expects actual network use to make later improvements clearer.

questions: what was rfc 73's response to the protocol change
why did crocker recommend waiting to change the protocol
what did sites say about the proposed change
subtitle: A response recommending implementation before nonessential protocol changes.

tldr.problem: A suggested protocol modification was under discussion while sites were beginning to implement the existing protocol.
tldr.mechanism: Steve Crocker supports delaying the suggestion unless necessity requires it, so sites can implement the protocol and gain experience using the network.
tldr.outcome: The note records a policy view and the results of a poll of several sites; it does not record a formal decision.

today: The unit metadata records RFC 73 as Unknown and lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. Its text is a response dated 25 September 1970 to a protocol-change suggestion.

sections.title: Delay Changes Not Required by Necessity
sections.content:
Steve Crocker calls the suggestion in RFC 67 a good one but says he would delay it. His current policy is to encourage the most rapid implementation of the protocol in document 1.

He argues that the group should gain experience using the network before making changes that are not required by necessity.
sections.plainLanguage: The author considers the suggested change reasonable, but recommends waiting unless it is necessary. He wants sites to build and use the existing protocol first.

sections.title: Views from Network Sites
sections.content:
Crocker says he polled several sites about the suggestion. Sites with NCP implementations underway tended to agree with delaying the change, while sites that were further behind tended to want the suggested change.

The note reports these views but does not say that the poll produced a binding decision.
sections.plainLanguage: Sites already implementing the NCP tended to favor waiting. Sites further behind tended to favor the proposed change.

sections.title: Improvements After Use
sections.content: The author says changes will be needed to improve efficiency, flexibility and reliability. He expects clearer ideas about those changes to emerge from using the network.
sections.plainLanguage: The author expects the protocol to need improvements. He thinks actual use will help the group identify them more clearly.
